title: War as Peace
subtitle: Seeing social force as Einstein saw physical force

blocks.html: Standing still, we used to feel the forces of our bodies and the Earth oppose each other. Falling was acceleration. When we threw rocks and when we fired cannonballs, they did not fly straight—they curved toward the ground.

Today, we are aware (on some level) that our intuitive picture is just a convenience. Inside the close-up concept, falling is stillness; standing is accelerating upward; projectiles do fly straight; and, while they fly, space flows (from our “timelike” point of view).

The single most important question now facing political, economic, and psychological theory is whether to seek the end of war. Is war a permanent feature of human life? Is world peace possible? Desirable? Is warfare itself evil?

War—with Nature, other people, and eventually our own bodies—is our primordial background, the shadow that conceives the coercive power of the state, the variable monetary value of time, the masses of dangerous and damaged personalities.
If war can one day be forgotten, then we could finally hope to live in a world of choice and diversity, honest leaders, sound currency, voluntary trade, and sound human minds.
I think not. I want to put forward some evidence that war is here to stay and a theoretical movement for social theory to parallel the physical theory of general relativity.
